title: Allowed-sequence networks grow fast for class 3 and 4, slowly for 1 and 2

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Allowed-sequence networks grow fast for class 3 and 4, slowly for 1 and 2

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: As cellular automata evolve, the set of cell sequences that can occur generally becomes progressively restricted; the finite networks describing these sets stay simple (about t^2 nodes after t steps) for class 1 and 2 rules but grow at least exponentially for most class 3 and 4 rules, apart from surjective rules started from all possible sequences.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Indeed, this kind of rapid increase in network complexity is a general characteristic of most class 3 and 4 rules.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “The Notion of Attractors” (from p. 275), p. 279. Scope: one-dimensional cellular automata and the regular languages of their configurations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The network size is precise once the regular-language construction is fixed, and representative rules can be computed. Coverage sufficient for “most class 3 and 4 rules” and asymptotic lower bounds is much harder.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct minimal finite automata recognizing length-unbounded configurations reachable after t steps and measure node count versus t for classified rules. Fit polynomial and exponential growth models and separately identify surjective rules.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite t does not establish asymptotic growth.

Automaton minimization becomes exponentially expensive.

Class labels and “most” require sampling choices.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.5

operationalizability: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The network in the text is the automaton for the regular language of admissible configurations, which is computable for elementary rules at small t, and the surjective exceptions are a known finite list. Exponential growth is self-limiting: the interesting class 3 and 4 networks are exactly those a small team cannot expand far. Early-time counts test the split on elementary rules and leave most class 3 and 4 rules, and large t, open.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Build the regular language of length-unrestricted configurations after t steps and count states in its minimal automaton. Growth near t^2 for class 1 and 2 rules, and at least exponential growth for non-surjective class 3 and 4 rules, would support the split over the times that can be built.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Surjective rules started from all sequences are real exceptions and must be separated.

The subset construction becomes infeasible in the exponential regime the claim describes.

Polynomial versus exponential is ambiguous at the small times one can finish.
